arxiv-2011-05423.title: Analysis and optimization of certain parallel Monte Carlo methods in the low temperature limit
arxiv-2011-05423.creator: Paul Dupuis, Guo-Jhen Wu
arxiv-2011-05423.description: Abstract Metastability is a formidable challenge to Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. In this paper we present methods for algorithm design to meet this challenge. The design problem we consider is temperature selection for the infinite swapping scheme, which is the limit of the widely used parallel tempering scheme obtained when the swap rate tends to infinity.

arxiv-2102-08968.title: Gravitational wave cosmology I: high frequency approximation Preprint: YITP-21-11, IPMU21-0011
arxiv-2102-08968.creator: Jared Fier 1, Xiongjun Fang 2, Bowen Li 1, Shinji Mukohyama 3,4, Anzhong Wang 1, Tao Zhu 5,6
arxiv-2102-08968.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jared Fier 1, Xiongjun Fang 2, Bowen Li 1, Shinji Mukohyama 3,4, Anzhong Wang 1, Tao Zhu 5,6. In this paper, we systematically study gravitational waves (GWs) first produced by remote compact astrophysical sources and then propagating in our inhomogeneous universe through cosmic distances, before arriving at detectors.

arxiv-2105-06886.title: Long-range Ising interactions mediated by λ ​ ϕ 4 \lambda\phi^{4} fields: probing the renormalisation of sound in crystals of trapped ions
arxiv-2105-06886.creator: G. Martín-Vázquez, G. Aarts, M. Müller, A. Bermudez
arxiv-2105-06886.description: Abstract The generating functional of a self-interacting scalar quantum field theory (QFT), which contains all the relevant information about real-time dynamics and scattering experiments, can be mapped onto a collection of multipartite-entangled two-level sensors via an interferometric protocol that exploits a specific set of source functions.

arxiv-2204-13778.title: Inferring Implicit Relations in Complex Questions with Language Models
arxiv-2204-13778.creator: Uri Katz Mor Geva Jonathan Berant
arxiv-2204-13778.description: Abstract A prominent challenge for modern language understanding systems is the ability to answer implicit reasoning questions, where the required reasoning steps for answering the question are not mentioned in the text explicitly. In this work, we investigate why current models struggle with implicit reasoning question answering (QA) tasks, by decoupling inference of reasoning steps from their execution.

arxiv-2207-05507.title: Fragmented atomic shell around S187 H ii region and its interaction with molecular and ionized gas 2021 Fragmented atomic shell around S187 H ii region and its interaction with molecular and ionized gas – 24
arxiv-2207-05507.creator: Petr Zemlyanukha, Igor I. Zinchenko, Evgeny Dombek, Lev E. Pirogov, Anastasiia Topchieva, Gilles Joncas, Lokesh K. Dewangan, Devendra K. Ojha, Swarna K. Ghosh
arxiv-2207-05507.description: Abstract The environment of S187, a nearby H ii region (1.4 ± \pm 0.3 kpc), is analyzed. A surrounding shell has been studied in the H i line, molecular lines, and also in infrared and radio continua. We report the first evidence of a clumpy HI environment in its photodissociation region.

arxiv-2311-13979.title: Location-Domination Type Problems Under the Mycielski Construction Thanks: This work was sponsored by a public grant overseen by the French National Research Agency as part of the “Investissements d’Avenir” through the IMobS3 Laboratory of Excellence (ANR-10-LABX-0016) and the IDEX-ISITE initiative
arxiv-2311-13979.creator: Silvia M. Bianchi, Dipayan Chakraborty, Yanina Lucarini, Annegret K. Wagler
arxiv-2311-13979.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Silvia M. Bianchi, Dipayan Chakraborty, Yanina Lucarini, Annegret K. Wagler. We consider the following variants of the classical minimum dominating set problem in graphs: locating-dominating set, locating total-dominating set and open locating-dominating set. All these problems are known to be hard for general graphs. A typical line of attack, therefore, is to either determine the minimum cardinalities of such sets in general or to establish bounds on these minimum cardinalities in special graph classes.

arxiv-2402-18968.title: Ambisonics Networks - The Effect Of Radial Functions Regularization
arxiv-2402-18968.creator: Bar Shaybet, Anurag Kumar, Vladimir Tourbabin, Boaz Rafaely
arxiv-2402-18968.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bar Shaybet, Anurag Kumar, Vladimir Tourbabin, Boaz Rafaely. Ambisonics, a popular format of spatial audio, is the spherical harmonic (SH) representation of the plane wave density function of a sound field. Many algorithms operate in the SH domain and utilize the Ambisonics as their input signal. The process of encoding Ambisonics from a spherical microphone array involves dividing by the radial functions, which may amplify noise at low frequencies.

arxiv-2411-07836.title: Robust estimation of carbon dioxide airborne fraction under measurement errors
arxiv-2411-07836.creator: J. Eduardo Vera-Valdés *, Charisios Grivas
arxiv-2411-07836.description: Abstract This paper discusses the effect of measurement errors in the estimation of the carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) airborne fraction. We are the first to present regression-based estimates and standard errors that are robust to measurement errors for the extended model, the preferred specification to estimate the CO 2 airborne fraction.

arxiv-2502-15427.title: Adversarial Prompt Evaluation: Systematic Benchmarking of Guardrails Against Prompt Input Attacks on LLMs
arxiv-2502-15427.creator: Giulio Zizzo Giandomenico Cornacchia Kieran Fraser Muhammad Zaid Hameed, Beat Buesser, Mark Purcell, Pin-Yu Chen, Kush Varshney
arxiv-2502-15427.description: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) become integrated into everyday applications, ensuring their robustness and security is increasingly critical. In particular, LLMs can be manipulated into unsafe behaviour by prompts known as jailbreaks. The variety of jailbreak styles is growing, necessitating the use of external defences known as guardrails.

arxiv-2502-17375.title: The adaptation property in non-equilibrium chemical systems
arxiv-2502-17375.creator: E. Franco, J. J. L. Velázquez
arxiv-2502-17375.description: Abstract The goal of this paper is to understand if the property of adaptation, which is a typical property of many biochemical systems, can be achieved only by biological systems that actively consume energy or if it can be achieved also by passive systems.

Humanitarian logistics literature has extensively studied epidemic impacts; however, there exists a research gap in understanding of pandemic...

pmc-10559171.title: Integrating network pharmacology and experimental verification strategies to reveal the active ingredients and molecular mechanism of Tenghuang Jiangu Capsule against osteoporosis
pmc-10559171.creator: Miao Li, Hongyu Tang, Yuanhao Hu, Songtao Li, Pan Kang, Baihao Chen, Shaocong Li, Meng Zhang, Haibin Wang, Shaochuan Huo
pmc-10559171.description: Tenghuang Jiangu Capsule (THJGC) is a Chinese herbal formula used for the treatment of osteoporosis and osteoarthritis in China, but its mechanism for treating osteoporosis is not clear. The aim of this study was to investigate the therapeutic effect of THJGC on osteoporosis and its intrinsic mechanism through network pharmacology and experimental validation.

pmc-10660866.creator: Hellen Cris Araújo Souza, Maycon Douglas Araújo Souza, Cássio Silva Sousa, Edilanne Katrine Amparo Viana, Sabrina Kelly Silva Alves, Alex Oliveira Marques, Arthur Serejo Neves Ribeiro, Vanessa de Sousa do Vale, Muhammad Torequl Islam, João Antônio Leal de Miranda, Marcelo da Costa Mota, Jefferson Al

Bioactive compounds of Moringa oleifera exhibited activity against SARS-CoV-2.Computational approaches to studying the antiviral activity of natural compounds against SARS-CoV-2 might be a time- and money-saving option in the drug discovery and development process. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-11314412.title: Cancer Treatment Using Nanofibers: A Review
pmc-11314412.creator: Muhammad Qamar Khan, Muhammad Abbas Alvi, Hafiza Hifza Nawaz, Muhammad Umar, David Cornu
pmc-11314412.description: Currently, the number of patients with cancer is expanding consistently because of a low quality of life. For this reason, the therapies used to treat cancer have received a lot of consideration from specialists. Numerous anticancer medications have been utilized to treat patients with cancer.

pmc-11462193.title: Ablation and laparoscopic adrenalectomy: Balancing efficacy and safety in the treatment of benign adrenal gland tumors: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11462193.creator: Benjamin Skribek, Anett Szabó, Júlia Ács, Péter Hegyi, Péter Mátrai, Péter Nyirády, Nándor Ács, Attila Majoros, Pál Ákos Deák
pmc-11462193.description: BackgroundAldosterone-producing adenomas cause hypertension in 5–10 % of cases. Laparoscopic adrenalectomy is the gold standard treatment for early-stage adrenal gland tumors, but minimally invasive procedures, such as ablative techniques can also be applied. Therefore, we aimed to compare laparoscopic adrenalectomy and ablation techniques in terms of efficacy and safety in the treatment of benign adrenal gland tumors.

pmc-11533329.title: Transparency and translucency indices for 1,525 pictograms from the Aragonese Portal of Augmentative and Alternative Communication
pmc-11533329.creator: Emiliano Díez, Antonio M. Díez-Álamo, María A. Alonso, Dominika Z. Wojcik, Angel Fernandez
pmc-11533329.description: This study investigated the transparency and translucency of 1,525 pictograms from the Aragonese Portal of Augmentative and Alternative Communication (ARASAAC). A total of 521 participants took part in tasks that involved providing the word that best described the meaning of a pictogram or rating the relationship between a pictogram and a verbal label.

pmc-11621002.title: Does internet use promote the health of empty-nest older adults in rural China? The mediating role of social participation using a propensity score matching approach
pmc-11621002.creator: Li Shen, Yawen Zheng, Mengting Wang, Hong Pan, Wenqian Jian, Xudong Yang, Wei Wang, Li Chen
pmc-11621002.description: BackgroundThe rapid growth of internet use among older adults in rural China offers a unique opportunity to examine its potential impact on their health. This study seeks to explore the relationship between internet use and the emotional, physical, and cognitive health of empty-nest older adults in rural China, while also considering the mediating role of social participation in this relationship.

pmc-12436384.title: Population pharmacokinetic modeling of dexmedetomidine nasal spray in Chinese adults
pmc-12436384.creator: Yuanyuan Huang, Sheng Xu, Nassim Djebli, Hao Jiang, Guoping Yang
pmc-12436384.description: ObjectiveThe main objective was to build and qualify a population pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model for dexmedetomidine nasal spray in Chinese adults and explore the covariates affecting the PopPK model parameters.MethodsA population pharmacokinetic model was developed based on the results of 1,225 blood concentration points from 196 healthy volunteers (HV) and patients in phase I and phase III studies.

pmc-12563932.title: Effects of a Food-Shaping Agent on the Texture and Palatability of Hospital-Pureed Meat: A Comparison of Subjective and Instrumental Assessments
pmc-12563932.creator: Ya-Ting Kuo, Pey-Rong Chen, Suh-Ching Yang
pmc-12563932.description: (1) Background: This study compared subjective and objective texture classifications of hospital-provided pureed meat dishes and evaluated the impact of adding a food-shaping agent on the consistency of the food. (2) Methods: In total, 18 common pureed meat dishes (pork, chicken, and fish) from a medical center were tested.

pmc-13173396.title: Evaluation of the Effects of 50 Hz Magnetic Field Exposure on the Human Hematopoietic System in Humanized Mice
pmc-13173396.creator: Masayuki Takahashi, Izumi Nishimura, Toshihiko Toda
pmc-13173396.description: Accumulating evidence from experimental animal studies is essential for clarifying the causal relationship between exposure to power‐frequency magnetic fields (MFs) and childhood leukemia. In this study, we developed a 50 Hz MF exposure system for experimental animals. To ensure uniform whole‐body exposure of multiple animals placed at the center of the coil, we fabricated a Merritt‐type coil.

pmc-13350814.title: Initial demonstration of a quantum heat engine based on dissipation-engineered superconducting circuits
pmc-13350814.creator: Tuomas Uusnäkki, Timm Mörstedt, Wallace Teixeira, Miika Rasola, Mikko Möttönen
pmc-13350814.description: Quantum heat engines require precise control over thermal reservoirs and the energies of the quantum working medium. Although superconducting circuits enable accurate engineering of controlled quantum systems, they have not yet been employed to experimentally realize a cyclic quantum heat engine.

pmc-13364589.title: A rare case report: The impact of Mycobacterium colombiense localized infections in a person living with HIV/AIDS
pmc-13364589.creator: Lurun Wang, Wenbing Lai, Yuze Liu, Jinwen Huang, Haixia Jing, Xianhui Wang
pmc-13364589.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Individuals living with HIV/AIDS may be more susceptible to various opportunistic infections due to an immunocompromised status, which can result in diverse clinical manifestations. Among potential pathogens, Mycobacterium colombiense—a slow-growing bacterium—could pose a significant threat to such patients. Here, we present the case of a 46-year-old woman with HIV/AIDS who developed an initial dark red plaque that gradually expanded, accompanied by persistent sinus tracts and suppuration. Interestingly, the patient reported no pain or itching.

pmc-13365245.title: Elovanoid neuroprotection targets cell transcriptomics and proteomics to sustain synaptic integrity after brain injury
pmc-13365245.creator: Brian L Giles, Surjyadipta Bhattacharjee, Jeff X Ji, Pranab K Mukherjee, Ludmila Belayev, Carlos M Vieira, Nicolas G Bazan
pmc-13365245.description: Traumatic brain injury (TBI), a leading cause of death and disability, is the largest non-genetic, non-aging-related contributor to cognitive impairments. Currently, there are limited effective therapies to protect neurons after acute brain injury. Our results suggest that intranasal-delivered (IN) elovanoid (ELV) shortly after TBI elicits neuroprotection that involves synaptic and mitochondrial pathways that mediate neuroprotection.
